anomalies.observed: The netlist contains two ATtiny microcontrollers, U1 ATtiny45-20P and U4 ATtiny13V-10S, wired pin-to-pin on the same functional nets. For example, the AVR-ISP MISO net connects J2.1 to both U1.6 and U4.6 (PB1), and the SCK net connects J2.3 to both U1.7 and U4.7 (PB2).
anomalies.expected: The specification describes a single ATtiny-driven fan controller, and the ISP wiring matches ATtiny13 SPI pins (PB0/PB1/PB2). If an ATtiny45 were intended, its ISP MISO/SCK pins are PB3/PB4, not PB1/PB2; otherwise only one MCU footprint should be connected and populated.
anomalies.impact: If both MCU footprints are populated, two microcontrollers drive the same lines, causing contention and unpredictable behavior. If U1 is used, it cannot be programmed through the existing AVR-ISP header because the header is wired for ATtiny13 MISO/SCK on PB1/PB2 rather than ATtiny45 MISO/SCK on PB3/PB4.

parsed.summary: The design files show two ATtiny MCUs connected in parallel, with ISP signals matching only the ATtiny13 pinout, which deviates from the intended single ATtiny fan controller and can cause contention or unprogrammability.
